source.text: tantrasāra, caturdaśam āhnikam atha putrakadīkṣāvidhiḥ // abhts_14.1 sa ca vistīrṇaḥ tantrālokāt avadhāryaḥ // abhts_14.2 saṃkṣiptas tu ucyate // abhts_14.3 samayyantaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā tṛtīye 'hni triśūlābje maṇḍale sāmudāyikaṃ yāgaṃ pūjayet tatra bāhyaparivāraṃ dvāradevatācakraṃ ca bahiḥ pūjayet tato maṇḍalapūrvabhāge aiśakoṇāt ārabhya āgneyāntaṃ paṅktikrameṇa gaṇapatiṃ guruṃ paramaguruṃ parameṣṭhinaṃ pūrvācāryān yoginīcakraṃ vāgīśvarīṃ kṣetrapālaṃ ca pūjayet // abhts_14.4 tata ājñāṃ samucitām ādāya śūlamūlāt prabhṛti sitakamalāntaṃ samastam adhvānaṃ nyasya arcayet tato madhyame triśūle madhyārāyāṃ bhagavatī śrīparābhaṭṭārikā bhairavanāthena saha vāmārāyāṃ tathaiva śrīmadaparā dakṣiṇārāyāṃ śrīparāparā dakṣiṇe triśūle madhye śrīparāparā vāme triśūle madhye śrīmadaparā dve tu yathāsvam // abhts_14.5 evaṃ sarvasthānādhiṣṭhātṛtve bhagavatyāḥ sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ tadadhiṣṭhānāt bhavati iti // abhts_14.6 tato madhyaśūlamadhyārāyāṃ samastaṃ devatācakraṃ lokapālāstraparyantam abhinnatayaiva pūjayet tadadhiṣṭhānāt sarvatra pūjitam // abhts_14.7 tataḥ kumbhe kalaśe maṇḍale agnau svātmani ca abhedabhāvanayā pañcādhikaraṇam anusaṃdhiṃ kuryāt tataḥ parameśvarādvayarasabṛṃhitena puṣpādinā viśeṣapūjāṃ kuryāt // abhts_14.8 kiṃ bahunā tarpaṇanaivedyaparipūrṇaṃ vittaśāṭhyavirahito yāgasthānaṃ kuryāt // abhts_14.9 asati vitte tu mahāmaṇḍalayāgo na kartavya eva // abhts_14.10 paśūṃś ca jīvato nivedayet // abhts_14.11 te 'pi hi evam anugṛhītā bhavanti iti kāruṇikatayā paśuvidhau na vicikitset // abhts_14.12 tato 'gnau parameśvaraṃ tilājyādibhiḥ saṃtarpya tadagre 'nyaṃ paśuṃ vapāhomārthaṃ kuryāt devatācakraṃ tadvapayā tarpayet punar maṇḍalaṃ pūjayet tataḥ parameśvaraṃ vijñapya sarvābhinnasamastaṣaḍadhvaparipūrṇam ātmānaṃ bhāvayitvā śiṣyaṃ puro 'vasthitaṃ kuryāt // abhts_14.13 parokṣadīkṣāyāṃ jīvanmṛtarūpāyām agre taṃ dhyāyet tadīyāṃ vā pratikṛtiṃ darbhagomayādimayīm agre sthāpayet // abhts_14.14 tathāvidhaṃ śiṣyam arghapātravipruṭprokṣitaṃ puṣpādibhiś ca pūjitaṃ kṛtvā samastam adhvānaṃ taddehe nyaset // abhts_14.15 tata itthaṃ vicārayet bhogecchoḥ śubhaṃ na śodhayet // abhts_14.16 mumukṣos tu śubhāśubham ubhayam api // abhts_14.17 nirbījāyāṃ tu samayapāśān api śodhayet sā ca āsannamaraṇasya atyantamūrkhasyāpi kartavyā iti parameśvarājñā tasyāpi tu gurudevatāgnibhaktiniṣṭhatvamātrāt siddhiḥ // abhts_14.18 atra ca sarvatra vāsanāgrahaṇam eva bhedakam mantrāṇāṃ vāsanānuguṇyena tattatkāryakāritvāt // abhts_14.19 evaṃ vāsanābhedam anusaṃdhāya mukhyamantraparāmarśaviśeṣeṇa samastam adhvānaṃ svadehagataṃ śivādvayabhāvanayā śodhayet // abhts_14.20 evaṃ krameṇa pādāṅguṣṭhāt prabhṛti dvādaśāntaparyantaṃ svātmadehasvātmacaitanyābhinnīkṛtadehacaitanyasya śiṣyasya āsādya tatraiva anantānandasarasi svātantryaiśvaryasāre samastecchājñānakriyāśaktinirbharasamastadevatācakreśvare samastādhvabharite cinmātrāvaśeṣaviśvabhāvamaṇḍale tathāvidharūpaikīkāreṇa śiṣyātmanā saha ekībhūto viśrāntim āsādayet ity evaṃ parameśvarābhinno 'sau bhavati // abhts_14.21 tato yadi bhogecchuḥ syāt tato yatraiva tattve bhogecchā asya bhavati tatraiva samastavyastatayā yojayet // abhts_14.22 tadanantaraṃ śeṣavṛttaye parameśvarasvabhāvāt jhaṭiti prasṛtaṃ śuddhatattvamayaṃ deham asmai cintayet ity eṣā samastapāśaviyojikā dīkṣā // abhts_14.23 tataḥ śiṣyo guruṃ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūrvavat pūjayet // abhts_14.24 tato 'gnau śiṣyasya vidhiṃ kuryāt śrīparāmantraḥ amukasyāmukaṃ tattvaṃ śodhayāmi iti svāhāntaṃ pratitattvaṃ tisra āhutayaḥ ante pūrṇā vauṣaḍantā // abhts_14.25 evaṃ śivāntatattvaśuddhiḥ tato yojanikoktakrameṇa pūrṇāhutiḥ // abhts_14.26 bhogecchoḥ bhogasthāne yojanikārtham aparā śuddhatattvasṛṣṭyartham anyā // abhts_14.27 tato guroḥ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjanam ity eṣā putrakadīkṣā // abhts_14.28 yatra vartamānam ekaṃ varjayitvā bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca karma śudhyati // abhts_14.29

## tsa14-p01
Now son-initiation-course, fourteenth ahnika. Putraka initiation, extensive, is to be learned from Tantrāloka; condensed is stated. (14.1–14.3) Having done to samayin-end the course, on third day in trident-lotus maṇḍala communal rite one should worship; outer retinue and door-god-wheel outside; then in maṇḍala-east from northeast to southeast in rows: Gaṇapati, teacher, supreme teacher, highest, former teachers, yoginī-wheel, speech-lady, field-guardian. (14.4) Taking fit command, from trident-root to white-lotus-end the whole course placed, worship: middle trident middle spoke goddess Parā with Bhairava-lord, left Aparā, right Parāparā, south middle Parāparā, left middle Aparā, two as own. (14.5) In goddess all-place-presiding, all is full; from its presiding it becomes. (14.6) In middle-trident-middle-spoke the whole god-wheel to weapon-guardian-end as undivided worship; from its presiding, everywhere worshipped. (14.7) In jar, pitcher, maṇḍala, fire, self, by nondifference-contemplation five-based linking; then with Lord-nonduality-rasa-swollen flower-offering special worship. (14.8) In short: libation-food-full, unstingy rite-house. (14.9) Without wealth, no great maṇḍala at all. (14.10) Living animals offer — thus graced they become; compassionately in animal-course do not doubt. (14.11–14.12) In fire the Lord ghee-sesame fed, second animal for fat-offering, wheel fat-fed, maṇḍala re-worshipped; Lord entreated, whole-undivided-six-course-full self contemplated, pupil set before. (14.13) In unseen living-dead initiation, meditate him before, or place kuśa-dung image. (14.14) Sprinkled/worshipped pupil: whole course placed in his body. (14.15) Consider: enjoyer's auspicious do not purify; liberation-wisher's both; in seedless purify even time-bonds — dying and utter fool too, by Lord's command, devotion-only succeeding. (14.16–14.18) Everywhere latency-grasping alone distinguishes, since mantras work by latency-fitness. (14.19) Reflecting latency-difference, by chief-mantra-grasping purify own-body-gone whole course in Śiva-nonduality: toe to twelve-end, pupil's self-body-consciousness-nondifferent reached, in bliss-lake, lordship-pith, all-power-full wheel-lord, consciousness-remainder circle, one-made with pupil-self, rest attaining — thus Lord-nondifferent he becomes. (14.20–14.21) Enjoyer joined where his wish lies; remaining conduct: sudden pure-principle body contemplated — all-bond-releasing initiation. (14.22–14.23) Pupil worships teacher. (14.24) In fire the pupil's rite: "Parā-mantra, so-and-so's so-principle I purify" + svāhā, thrice per principle, vauṣaḍa full at end. (14.25) Thus Śiva-end purity; then joining full-offering. (14.26) For enjoyer a second for joining-place, a third for pure creation. (14.27) Teacher gifted — this is son-initiation. (14.28) Wherein, leaving present one, past and future karma is purified. (14.29)

## tsa14-p01 — the son's initiation
The son's rite, full form in the Tantrāloka, short form here. Samayin-course done: on day three, communal worship in the trident-lotus — retinue and door-gods outside, then rows east to southeast: Gaṇapati, teachers past and present, yoginīs, Speech-lady, field-lord. Command taken, the whole course laid from trident-root to white lotus: center Parā with Bhairava, left Aparā, right Parāparā (south and left tridents likewise); goddess presiding everywhere makes everything full; the whole wheel to the weapon-guardians worshipped undivided — presided, all worshipped. Jar, pitcher, circle, fire, self linked in five, then special worship swollen with nonduality's rasa. No stinting; no wealth, no great circle. Living beasts offered — graced thereby, doubt not, for pity's sake. Fire fed ghee and sesame for the Lord, a second beast for fat, wheel fat-fed, circle re-honored; Lord entreated; self seen whole-six-courses-full; pupil set forth. For the far-off (living-dead), picture him — or a grass-and-dung stand-in. Sprinkle and honor him, lay the whole course in his body. Then judge: enjoyer — cleanse the bright only; freedom-seeker — bright and dark; seedless — even time-bonds, dying or dullest, by the Lord's order, devotion alone availing. Mantras work by fit with latency — grasp that difference always. By the chief mantra's grasp, cleanse the body-gone whole course in Śiva-oneness: toe to twelve-end, pupil's body-consciousness reached as your own, in bliss's lake, lordship's pith, the all-powered wheel, the circle where world is consciousness-remnant — one with the pupil-self, rest: Lord-undivided he becomes. Join enjoyers where they hunger; then picture a sudden pure-principle body for the conduct that remains — the initiation loosing every bond. Pupil honors teacher; fire-rite per pupil ("Parā-mantra — so-and-so's so-principle I cleanse" + svāhā, thrice a principle, vauṣaḍa full): Śiva-end purity, joining full-offerings (a second for the enjoyer's station, a third for pure creation). Gifts to the teacher seal it: son-initiation, washing past and future deeds, the present kept.
